newsitem.title: USA: Banc One agrees to buy First USA for $6.6 billion.
newsitem.headline: Banc One agrees to buy First USA for $6.6 billion.

text.p: Banc One Corp. said Monday that it agreed to buy First USA Inc. for about $6.6 billion in a stock transaction that will double its U.S. credit card operations and open up avenues for new business.
Banc One said its combination with First USA will form the third-largest credit card operation in the country with about 32 million cardholders and assets of $35 billion.
It said it agreed to pay 1.1659 shares of Banc One common stock for each share of Dallas-based First USA, which is one of the four biggest banks in the country that specialise in credit card lending.
Based on Banc One's Monday trading price of $41.625, which was down $3.50 from Friday, the deal would be worth about $6.64 billion.
While Wall Street analysts noted that Banc One was paying a steep premium for First USA, they said the deal had potential to produce big returns for Banc One, which is based in Columbus, Ohio.

"It gives them a tremendous amount of power in writing new business, particulary asset-backed securities," Robert Bonelli, executive vice president at Ernst & Co., said, referring to credit card portfolios that are securitized and sold to third parties.

"I wouldn't be looking at the combination squeezing out expenses. Instead, I would look at the degree of critical mass that will allow them to do a large amount of new business," Bonelli said. "It's a good deal. It's an exciting deal. There is going to be a lot of value for shareholders going forward."
Analysts said, however, that Banc One's share price slipped in early trading due to concerns about a reduction in earnings as a result of the merger.
Analysts agreed that Banc One was paying a steep price -- more than six times First USA's book value of about $8.50 a share and more than 20 times earnings.
But they also said that well-publicised problems in credit card lending, chiefly rising delinquency and charge-off rates, did not detract from the profitability of the business.
Nancy Bush of Brown Brothers Harriman said profitability in cards was about twice that in banking generally.
As part of the deal, Banc One also will buy First USA Paymentech Inc., a credit card payments processing business of which 57 percent is owned by First USA.
First USA has 16 million cardholders and managed receivables worth $22.4 billion while Banc One also has 16 million cardholders and $12.6 billion in managed receivables.
The deal is expected to be completed by May 31.
Bonelli said while the percentage of credit card debt that banks are forced to write off has been creeping up, "consumers are managing their credit today better than ever before."
He said with credit card rates of around 13.5 percent for the most creditworthy borrowers and rates in the 16 percent range for many people, the result is strong returns in the card business.
A key measure of profitiabilty in the banking industry, return on equity, is over 20 percent in card lending, Bonelli said.
